title: Food and wild plants
summary: Food is the lowest priority, and you should only eat a plant you can identify with certainty.

blocks.p: Food is the lowest priority: you can survive about three weeks without it. Don’t spend energy or risk poisoning chasing it early.

Only eat a plant you can identify with certainty. Water hemlock and poison hemlock are among the most poisonous plants in North America. Both can look like wild carrot (Queen Anne’s lace) or wild parsnip, people have died after eating poison hemlock roots as wild carrots or parsnips, and a small amount of water hemlock can kill.

blocks.label: Ate a plant or mushroom that might be poisonous

sections.h: Warning signs in plants you don’t know

list: Beans, bulbs or seeds inside pods
Carrot-, parsnip-, parsley- or dill-like leaves
An almond smell in the leaves or wood
Grain heads with pink, purple or black spurs

blocks.warn: These signs help you avoid many poisonous plants, not all of them. A plant that shows none of them is not safe to eat. Eat only a plant you have positively identified.

blocks.p: Some well-known edibles break these rules (blackberry canes have thorns), which is another reason positive identification matters more than any rule.

blocks.warn: Never eat a wild mushroom unless an expert has identified it. Poisonous mushrooms can look like edible ones, there is no field test that shows a mushroom is safe, and cooking does not destroy the poisons.

blocks.p: There are deliberately no drawings of plants here. Identify plants with a regional field guide that has real photographs, ideally after learning them from someone local.

blocks.label: Poison ivy, oak or sumac on the skin

list: Cattail: in wet ground. Young shoots can be eaten like asparagus, and the starchy roots and the pollen can be made into flour. Look-alikes: two poisonous irises grow in the same wet ground: yellow flag iris (invasive, on pond, lake and stream shores in New York) and the native blue flag iris (pond margins, wet meadows and marshes in the Northeast). Yellow flag iris is easily mistaken for cattail when it is not in flower. Cattail leaf bases are round; iris leaf bases are flat.
Wild blackberries and raspberries: if it looks like a store-bought blackberry or raspberry, it is one. They have no poisonous look-alikes.

Insects: grasshoppers, crickets, grubs and ants. Remove legs, wings and heads, and cook them fully. Skip insects that bite or sting, hairy or brightly coloured insects, caterpillars, smelly insects, spiders, and flies, ticks and mosquitoes.
Freshwater fish: cook them thoroughly, to 145°F inside, to kill parasites.

blocks.p: Pick plants well away from roads and from ground treated with pesticides or road salt, and wash them well.
